newsitem.title: UK: Leeson may gain from Barings collapse film - paper.
newsitem.headline: Leeson may gain from Barings collapse film - paper.

text.p: Nick Leeson, the Singapore-based trader blamed for the collapse of British bank Barings, could profit from a film of his life story, the Daily Telegraph reported on Friday.

As a result of a deal signed on Thursday, Leeson could have a comfortable life when he was released from the Singapore jail where he has served 18 months of a six-and-a-half year sentence for his part in Barings' downfall, said the paper.
"It is a substantial deal and should give him a more comfortable life when he gets out if the film is successful," the Telegraph quoted an unidentified source close to the negotiations as saying.
But Barings' administrators and liquidators have begun legal steps to ensure Leeson does not profit from his book "Rogue Trader" or a film version of it.

And bondholders who lost money as a result of the Barings collapse in February 1995 have also vowed to sue if Leeson, who ran up unauthorised derivatives trades totalling 800 million pounds ($1.3 billion), profited from the affair.
Barings was rescued by Dutch financial services giant Internationale Nederlanden Groep NV. ($ = 0.600 British Pounds)
